'The Five' comments on the Democratic Party's messaging and internal division as New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faces criticism over his policy agenda. The panel also discusses the arrests of Democratic Socialists of America members during protests against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in New York City and more.

A progressive congressional candidate backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was detained by the Israeli military in the West Bank on Wednesday morning.

Brad Lander, a former member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), scored an upset primary victory this year against Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y. But he was far from the New York City-area district this week, posting on X that he and others were being held by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) while on a trip to help Palestinian farmers harvest olives in disputed territory.

"I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis & volunteers. We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nehalim in the West Bank. The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know," Lander posted on X.

LIBERAL MS NOW WRITER CALLS MAMDANI PRIMARY SWEEP A 'GENUINELY SCARY NIGHT FOR NEW YORK CITY JEWS'

Zohran Mamdani, mayor of New York, and Brad Lander, former New York City comptroller and U.S. Democratic House candidate for New York, campaign during a primary election in New York, on Tuesday, June 23, 2026. (Adam Gray/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Lander is one of several anti-establishment candidates who Mamdani backed in New York City Democratic primaries this year. And he's not the first to get into a dust-up with law enforcement, either.

Socialist candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier, who defeated Congressional Hispanic Caucus Chairman Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y., in their primary race, said she was knocked to the ground by NYPD officers during a protest against federal immigration authorities shooting an illegal immigrant in the Bronx this month.

MAMDANI'S TEAM REPORTEDLY CLASHING WITH SOCIALIST CANDIDATE HE ENDORSED OVER ICE SHOOTING

Rabbis for Human Rights said congressional candidate Brad Lander was detained by Israeli law enforcement while in the West Bank this week. (Rabbis for Human Rights via X)

Lander is the former New York City comptroller and a former member of the DSA. He left the organization in 2023 in response to a rally members held the day after the Oct. 7 attacks by Hamas.

The group he was with in the West Bank, Rabbis for Peace, posted a photo of Lander and said he was detained "by Israeli police for standing with Palestinians during the olive harvest" along with others.

FAR-LEFT SURGE: MAMDANI-BACKED CANDIDATES OUST DEM ESTABLISHMENT INCUMBENTS

Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., during a canvass launch on the final weekend of early voting ahead of a primary election at Brooklyn Borough Hall in the Brooklyn borough of New York, on Saturday, June 20, 2026. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"The Palestinians whose land this is have a right to harvest it in peace," Lander, who is Jewish, said in a video posted by the group.

It's not clear if Lander has been released or what the terms of his detention are. Fox News Digital reached out to his campaign and to Mamdani's office for comment.

New York's 10th Congressional District is overwhelmingly Democratic, meaning he is all but assured to win his general election and come to Congress next year.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
NY congressional nominee Brad Lander says he was detained by the IDF in the West Bank

NY congressional candidate Brad Lander was detained by the IDF in the West Bank while harvesting olives alongside a group of rabbis and volunteers.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Lefty congressional nominee Brad Lander claimed Wednesday he was “detained” by the Israeli Defense Forces while working on an olive harvest in the West Bank.

Lander, the former Big Apple Comptroller who is running for Congress in the Nov. 3 election, posted a picture of himself glaring at the camera while onboard a bus with others who were on their phones and didn’t seem fazed.

“I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis & volunteers,” Lander posted on X. “We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nehalim in the West Bank.”

It is unclear if Lander, who is vying for New York’s 10th Congressional District seat, was doing anything else besides olive harvesting.

“The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know,” he added.

Lander had bested outgoing Rep. Dan Goldman (D-NY) in their June primary, mounting a challenge against him from the left. Lander, who is Jewish, has been an outspoken critic of Israel.

During his primary against Goldman and his unsuccessful run for mayor last year, Lander made Israel a top issue.

The Dem candidate has opposed unconditional military aid to the Jewish state and accused it of carrying out a genocide in the Gaza Strip after the bloody Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack.

“I think — with deep sadness — that Israel’s conduct in Gaza meets the definition of genocide. But even if you don’t, it’s profoundly inconsistent with the Jewish value that every one of those Palestinian kids were created in the image of God, just like ours,” he posted on X in June.

Lander also contended that “Israel can’t be a genuine democracy while it’s occupying the West Bank & Gaza.”

Rabbis for Human Rights, an Israeli human rights group, corroborated Lander’s claim about being detained and said 90 other volunteers were held by the IDF as well, while harvesting olives in Nahalin, outside Bethlehem.

Authorities designated the area they were working in as a military zone closed for a full day, according to the group.

Officials then checked the group for identification, despite the group’s leaders offering to leave voluntarily, according to Rabbis for Human Rights’ version of events.

“We came to accompany farmers to land they have not been able to reach in three years, and after two hours of quiet harvesting, large forces arrived and closed the area,” Acting executive director for Rabbis for Human Rights, Anton Goodman, said in a statement.

“No one could have known about this order in advance. Instead of protecting people working their own land, the army is removing them from it, and detaining those who came to stand beside them.”

Lander previously described his venture to the West Bank as a mission to help Palestinians with their harvest and to put the spotlight on conditions there.

Other lefty pols have had similar run-ins with Israeli authorities. In July, for example, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) said he and his group were detained by the Israelis for over an hour while in the Palestinian village of Khirbet Zanuta during a tour.
